messages:
mira (support): FYI ACME prod is seeing p99 jump to ~10s and a lot of 429s since 10:24 UTC. customer says embedding and chat endpoints both slow. repro steps below.

june (customer-success): escalated, they pasted logs and a curl example. can we triage ASAP? they are in EU region.

ravi (eng-runtime): looking at metrics now — cluster runtime-pool-eu request_queue_length spiked from ~20 -> 450 at 10:23. worker CPU/GPU utilization is moderate but KV cache hit rate dropped.

sam (eng-sre): that smells like admission control kicking in + head-of-line blocking. what did recent deploys change for concurrency/admit thresholds?

deploy-bot: deployment redwood/runtime-admission v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 rolled at 09:58 UTC (config: default_concurrency=80, burst_window_ms=150).

ravi (eng-runtime): aha — admission default_concurrency was lowered from 160 -> 80 in 2.4.0 to reduce memory pressure. seems we didn't account for the longer tail on this customer's workload.

mira (support): customer says they didn't change traffic pattern. traffic did spike ~10% but not enough to explain 10s p99 previously at 800ms.

sam (eng-sre): repro steps from customer (copied):
```
# repro curl
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-qa-large","input":"long prompt ~2k tokens"}' \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
They run many concurrent long requests -> KV cache cold starts + queuing.

ravi (eng-runtime): reading logs: `admission_controller: reject=true reason=concurrency_exceeded current=80 target=80`. Then many requests sit in the proxy queue and time out at 10s. sample log: 
```
[10:24:03] proxy: enqueueing req id=abc123 queue_len=312
[10:24:04] admission_controller: reject req id=abc123 reason=concurrency_exceeded
[10:24:14] proxy: request timeout id=abc123 elapsed=11.0s
```

alex (oncall): propose emergency mitigation sequence: 1) enable burst capacity / raise concurrency to 160 for runtime-pool-eu, 2) temporarily route heavy long-tail traffic to rwd-qa-medium variant, 3) scale up worker pool +10, 4) rollback admission change if needed. Can we do 1&3 now?

ravi (eng-runtime): applying quick config bump to admission controller for pool eu: `default_concurrency=160` and `burst_window_ms=250`. Pushing via `kubectl apply -f admission-eu-patch.yaml` (patching configmap).

infra-bot: scaling: replicas runtime-worker-eu from 12 -> 22 triggered by manual request from ravi.

deploy-bot: configmap redwood-runtime-admission updated by ravi at 10:39 UTC.

ravi (eng-runtime): also enabling routing fallback: add route rule to send requests with prompt_length>1500 to rwd-qa-medium for 30m. patch: `traffic.rules.long_prompt -> model: rwd-qa-medium`

mira (support): told customer we're applying mitigations; will ask them to retry a few requests and report back. :thumbsup:

june (customer-success): customer retried at 10:46: p95 dropped to 1.2s, p99 ~2.1s. they still see occasional 5-6s for the longest prompts but overall much better.

sam (eng-sre): good. we should create a postmortem: root cause = admission config change + underestimated KV cold-start effect for long-prompt workloads. short-term fixes applied: concurrency bump, pool scaling, routing fallback.

alex (oncall): follow-ups:
- add an alert for request_queue_length > 200 for >2m in any region
- add canary load tests for long-prompt workloads before admission/config changes
- revert the lowered default_concurrency in config if memory pressure not observed

ravi (eng-runtime): filing internal ticket and will schedule a controlled rollback/AB test of admission v2.4.0. also increasing KV cache warmup on scale events.

mira (support): customer confirmed in DM they're unblocked for now. closing escalation on our side but keeping ticket open until permanent fix. :white_check_mark:

june (customer-success): I'll send a short summary + timelines to the customer and include mitigation details.

sam (eng-sre): adding blameless postmortem item and linking to rollout notes. tagging follow-ups to product for rollout checklist.

ravi (eng-runtime): thanks all. will monitor p95/p99 dashboards for next 24h and post updates here. :eyes:
